fields.h1: Build an Employee Coaching Form Template That Follows Up
fields.hero_description: Build an employee coaching form template that logs each session, takes the employee's side, and books the next check-in.
fields.features_heading: What Each Coaching Session Leaves Behind
fields.features_subheading: A paper template stops at two signatures. Built with Emergent, the form keeps every session and its check-in on one record.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that change with the focus

Choose performance, attendance, conduct, or career growth at the top. The form then asks what that focus needs, such as the shift dates for attendance or a target role for growth.
fields.feature_2:
An observation box built for facts

Record the date, what you saw or heard, and what it affected, in separate fields. A manager writes the call ID and the 9-minute hold, and leaves out guesses about attitude or motive.
fields.feature_3:
A private link for the employee's side

Send the employee a link to the session after you save it. They write their own account in a field only they can edit, and the form asks both of you to sign before it closes.
fields.feature_4:
Action steps with an owner and a date

List each step as its own row with who does it and when it is due. Steps the manager owns, such as booking a training seat, sit beside the employee's, and every row has a status.
fields.feature_5:
A reminder before every check-in

Set the check-in date when you save the session, and the app emails the manager 3 days before it. The email says a check-in is due and links to the form, with no notes in it.
fields.feature_6:
Every session on file, in your own database

Keep each employee's sessions in a database you own, newest first, so the next talk starts from the last one. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Teams Run Coaching Sessions
fields.tab_content_1:
Call 4471 turns into two steps for Auberon

Fabiola Ebberley reviews call 4471 at Bramwick Broadband: 22 minutes, with a 9-minute hold while Auberon Vantreece looked for the refund rule. She logs the session before his shift ends. Two action steps follow. Auberon pins the refund guide, and Fabiola sits in on 3 of his calls next Tuesday.
fields.tab_content_2:
Niamh's side of it goes on the record

Ticket times at Wickerhame Kitchen hit 14 minutes on two Friday nights, and sous chef Konstanze Ferrandino logs a session with line cook Niamh Ottomer. Niamh opens her own link and writes that the fryer was down both nights. Konstanze adds a fryer check at opening, and both sign to confirm the talk took place.
fields.tab_content_3:
It ends with Xanthe choosing her own next step

Xanthe Kesterson wants to lead a release at Northcott Software within a year. Ulrika Stanwyck, her manager, runs the talk in four boxes that follow the GROW model. Under Reality, Xanthe has shipped 6 features but never run a release checklist. She weighs 3 options and picks the March checklist, with Ulrika as backup.
fields.tab_content_4:
Orlaith hears about each check-in 3 days early

Thirty days after each session at Saltcourt Logistics, shift lead Orlaith Gwendal holds a check-in, and a reminder email arrives 3 days before. At Tuesday's check-in, picker Jovita Ebrel has 2 of 3 action steps done. The forklift refresher is still open and carries into the next check-in, 30 days later.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Employee Coaching Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to build an employee coaching form template that records each talk and brings its action steps back at check-in.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Use four boxes for growth talks
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide that the form covers coaching only, and keep formal warnings on a separate form your HR team owns. That keeps each session about the work ahead. List the focus types you will use, such as performance, attendance, conduct, and growth.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the date, what the manager saw or heard, and its effect on the work. A useful entry names the call or the shift where it happened. Leave out labels such as lazy or careless, which describe a person instead of an event.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add a field for the employee's account, opened from a private link and written in their own words. Read it before you settle the action steps. A cause you did not know about, such as broken equipment, changes what the steps should be.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For career conversations, swap the observation fields for four boxes: Goal, Reality, Options, and Will. Ask the employee to fill in the options themselves. The Will box holds the one option they commit to, and it becomes the first action step.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Keep action steps to two or three
fields.howto_step_5_des: Cap each session at two or three action steps, each with one owner and a due date. Give the manager at least one step too, such as ordering a new headset or sitting in on a shift. Write every step as something a person can check off.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write one prompt with the focus types, the observation fields, the employee's link, the action step rows, and an email 3 days before each check-in. Emergent builds the form and its database. Change it later by describing the change in a new prompt.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it with last month's session
fields.howto_step_7_des: Enter a session from last month with two action steps and a check-in date a week out. Open the employee link and sign it with a short comment. Confirm the reminder arrives 3 days before the date, then delete the test session.

faq_plan.q: What is an employee coaching form template?
faq_plan.a: An employee coaching form template is a reusable record of one coaching conversation between a manager and an employee. It holds the focus of the talk, what the manager observed, the employee's response, the agreed action steps, and a date to check in.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an employee coaching form template?
faq_plan.a: List the fields you need, then describe them in one prompt: what each session covers, what the manager writes down, the action steps, and the check-in date. Emergent's AI form builder builds the form and the database behind it. Log one past session as a test before managers start using it.

faq_plan.q: How should a manager use an employee coaching form template in the meeting?
faq_plan.a: Fill in the form with the employee, not about them. Start from one specific observation and ask for their account before you suggest a fix. Agree on two or three steps with dates, and book the check-in before the meeting ends.

faq_plan.q: Can an employee coaching form template work for new hires?
faq_plan.a: Yes, with a lighter touch. Hold a short session in week two and another in week four, while the role is still new. Keep the start date and equipment list on a new employee form, and use the coaching form only for the conversations that follow.

faq_plan.q: How should observations be phrased on an employee coaching form template?
faq_plan.a: Write what happened, when, and what it affected, in a sentence the employee could check. Three of last week's five shifts started after 7:10 is an observation. Not committed to the schedule is a judgment of the person, and it belongs nowhere on the form.

faq_plan.q: Is an employee coaching form template the same as a written warning?
faq_plan.a: No. A coaching form records a conversation about improving or growing, with steps both people agree on. A written warning is formal discipline under the employer's own policy. Keep them on separate forms, and ask HR how your policy treats coaching records.

faq_plan.q: How is an employee coaching form template different from a client coaching intake?
faq_plan.a: A workplace coaching form records a manager's session with someone on their team, and it is about the job. A life coaching intake form is filled in by a client before a first session with a coach, and it covers personal goals. The employer keeps the first, and the coach keeps the second.

faq_plan.q: How often should check-ins on an employee coaching form template be scheduled?
faq_plan.a: Pick the date at the end of each session: two to four weeks out for a performance focus, and about 90 days for a career goal. Built with Emergent, the form can remind the manager by email ahead of each one.

faq_plan.q: Does an employee coaching form template need the employee's signature?
faq_plan.a: It should ask for one. A signature confirms the conversation took place, not that the employee agrees with every line. Give them space to write their own account before they sign, and their signature sits under their own words.

faq_plan.q: Who should see the records an employee coaching form template collects?
faq_plan.a: Limit it to the employee, their manager, and HR. Coaching notes are written to help one person improve, and they read differently to anyone outside that circle. With Emergent, the records sit in a database you own, and you decide who opens them.
